notes: Hook checked: after a power cut a latched DOL contactor's coil drops out and the holding contact opens, so the motor does not restart without an operator (research: Basic Motor Control, manual circuits and low-voltage protection). The hook stands as written.

oneBreath overclaim fixed: 'An AC motor works by making a magnetic field that turns and drags the rotor round a little behind it' is true of induction motors only (a synchronous motor keeps pace with its field; a universal motor runs on AC with brushes). Now 'An AC induction motor'.

oneBreath overclaim fixed: the starting method sets the starting current, while the running current follows the load. 'decides the current it draws' now reads 'decides the current it draws as it starts'.

oneBreath overclaim fixed: a DC motor's speed also depends on its supply voltage, so the field wiring decides how speed and torque change with load. Now 'How a DC motor's speed and torque change with load comes from how its field is wired'.

The rest of oneBreath (three-phase windings make the turning field alone; a single-phase motor needs a second winding, sometimes with a capacitor; a drive sets the frequency) agrees with the research and with ideas i1 to i8.
